theorem_title: The stored signed query equals the exact original prefix count
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.StoredReporting.storedQueryValue_eq_prefixQuery {h J k : ℕ} (P d : ℤ)
    (A : Finset α) (B : Finset β) (C : Finset γ)
    (a : α → ℤ) (b : β → ℤ) (c : γ → ℤ) (w : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawReporting.Wanted h J α)
    (pre : List (Finset (Fin (464 * h)))) (hk : k ≤ J) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.StoredReporting.storedQueryValue P d A B C a b c w k pre =
      (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawReporting.prefixQuery (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawIncidences.rawOn h J P d (A ×ˢ (B ×ˢ C)) a b c) w k pre : ℕ) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
For local dimensions $h,J$, level $k\le J$, integer modulus $P$ and shift $d$, finite original-index sets $A,B,C$ with maps $a,b,c$, wanted key $w$, and any proposed prefix, the stored-query integer value equals the natural raw-incidence prefix count. The raw domain uses the full original-index product $A\times B\times C$, so repeated values retain their original multiplicities.

This identity is the semantic bridge from the stored signed transform to the original-index count tested by reporting.
